# TFormVector <img class="product" src="media/b3d-20x14.png" alt="Blitz3D" title="Blitz3D" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Transforms](Blitz3D-Transforms)

</div>


```blitzbasic
TFormVector:Void x:Float32, y:Float32, z:Float32, source_entity:Int32, dest_entity:Int32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | In | Float32 | required | X of the vector in the source space. |
| `y` | In | Float32 | required | Y of the vector in the source space. |
| `z` | In | Float32 | required | Z of the vector in the source space. |
| `source_entity` | In | Int32 | required | Entity whose space the vector is in, or 0 for the world. |
| `dest_entity` | In | Int32 | required | Entity whose space the result should be in, or 0 for the world. |

## Description

Converts a direction from one space to another. Unlike [TFormPoint](TFormPoint) the position of the entities is ignored: only their rotation and scale are used, so a vector of length 1 turns into a longer one when the source entity is scaled. Read the result with [TFormedX](TFormedX), [TFormedY](TFormedY) and [TFormedZ](TFormedZ).

It is the right tool to find which way an entity moves when you push it forward: convert 0, 0, 1 from the entity to the world.
